Check every operational rating against its gaugings

Source: R/check_operational_ratings.R
check_operational_ratings.Rd

Runs compare_gaugings_to_rating() for every rating in an operational ratings export, against the gaugings of the station it is matched to, and collects the results in one place. It is the whole of the check in one call: build each rating as a table, link ratings to gauging stations, compare, and report both the findings and everything that could not be compared.

Nothing is excluded for being odd. A rating that cannot form a valid table, a rating whose station has no gaugings, a gauging station with no rating, and a row of the matching table that matched nothing are each listed with the reason, so the picture is complete and the unmatched part can be worked down.

By default every gauging of a matched station is compared with every rating of that station, whatever its dates. A station that has had several ratings over time will therefore show each rating against all of its gaugings. Set use_dates = TRUE to compare each rating only with gaugings taken while it was in force: from its start_date to its end_date, where an end date is missing, or is earlier than the start date (which the ratings export uses for "no end"), the rating is treated as still in force.

Usage

check_operational_ratings(
  gaugings,
  ratings,
  crosswalk = NULL,
  crosswalk_station = "FFFSLocID",
  crosswalk_reference = "Reference",
  direct = TRUE,
  use_dates = FALSE,
  tol_rel = 0.1,
  keep_gaugings = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

gaugings

A table from read_gaugings().

ratings

A table from read_operational_ratings().

crosswalk, crosswalk_station, crosswalk_reference, direct

As in match_stations().

use_dates

Logical. Compare each rating only with the gaugings taken while it was in force. Default FALSE. Needs observation_time in gaugings and start_date and end_date in ratings.

tol_rel

Numeric. Tolerance for share_within_tol, as in compare_gaugings_to_rating(). Default 0.10.

keep_gaugings

Logical. Also return every gauging with its residual against each rating it was compared with. Default FALSE: for a large archive this is a large table.

quiet

Logical. TRUE suppresses the summary message.

Value

A list with these elements.

  • ratings: one row per rating, with rating_key, station_id, station_name, n_limbs, status ("compared", "no gaugings" or "not a valid table"), reason (for a rating that is not a valid table), n_gaugings (compared), n_inside and n_extrapolated, n_limbs_with_gaugings, top_limb_has_gaugings, gauged_max_stage, median_residual_pct and share_within_tol over the gaugings inside the rating.

  • limbs: one row per limb of every compared rating, with rating_key, station_id, the columns of compare_gaugings_to_rating()'s limbs, and the export's flag and open_ended for that limb. flag is carried through so you can see whether it lines up with limbs that have no gaugings.

  • gaugings: the per-gauging results, or NULL unless keep_gaugings = TRUE.

  • matches: the list returned by match_stations().

  • problems: the ratings that are not valid tables, with the reason.

See also

match_stations(), compare_gaugings_to_rating(), read_gaugings(), read_operational_ratings().

Examples

# Two ratings and one archive of gaugings. Station "S1" has gaugings up to
# 2.3 m, so the top limb of its rating (to 4 m) has none. Station "S2" has
# a rating but no gaugings, and station "S3" has gaugings but no rating.
ratings <- data.frame(
  rating_key = rep(c("r1", "r2"), c(4, 2)), station_id = rep(c("S1", "S2"), c(4, 2)),
  station_name = rep(c("Bathford", "Skelton"), c(4, 2)),
  lower_level = c(0.30, 0.90, 1.70, 2.60, 0, 1), upper_level = c(0.90, 1.70, 2.60, 4.00, 1, 3),
  C = c(1.80000, 2.85549, 4.72355, 2.36038, 2, 2), a = c(0.10, 0.25, 0.55, 0.40, 0, 0),
  n = c(1.60, 1.90, 1.45, 2.20, 1.5, 1.5),
  flag = c(0, 0, 0, 3, 0, 0), open_ended = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
)
set.seed(3)
stage_m <- sort(runif(40, 0.3, 2.3))
gaugings <- data.frame(
  station_id = c(rep("S1", 40), rep("S3", 3)),
  stage_m = c(stage_m, 1, 1.5, 2),
  discharge_cms = c(apply_rating(FlodeRatingTable(table = data.table::as.data.table(ratings[1:4, 4:8])),
                                 stage_m)$discharge * exp(rnorm(40, sd = 0.04)), 3, 5, 8)
)
check <- check_operational_ratings(gaugings, ratings)
#> check_operational_ratings(): 2 ratings: 1 compared, 1 with no gaugings, 0 not valid tables.
#>   Limbs with no gaugings: 1 of 4 in compared ratings. Unmatched: 1 rating stations, 1 gauging stations.
check$ratings[, c("rating_key", "status", "n_gaugings", "median_residual_pct")]
#>    rating_key      status n_gaugings median_residual_pct
#>        <char>      <char>      <int>               <num>
#> 1:         r1    compared         40          -0.7291611
#> 2:         r2 no gaugings          0                  NA
check$limbs[, c("rating_key", "limb", "n_gaugings", "has_gaugings", "flag")]
#>    rating_key  limb n_gaugings has_gaugings  flag
#>        <char> <int>      <int>       <lgcl> <num>
#> 1:         r1     1         14         TRUE     0
#> 2:         r1     2         17         TRUE     0
#> 3:         r1     3          9         TRUE     0
#> 4:         r1     4          0        FALSE     3
check$matches$unmatched_gaugings
#>    station_id station_name n_gaugings
#>        <char>       <char>      <int>
#> 1:         S3         <NA>          3
